sections.title: Stating opinions
sections.content:
Advanced phrases for expressing what you think:
• In my view — In my view, education should be free for everyone.
• I'm firmly convinced that — I'm firmly convinced that technology improves learning.
• It seems to me that — It seems to me that the problem is communication.
• From my perspective — From my perspective, remote work has many benefits.
• I tend to think that — I tend to think that experience matters more than qualifications.

sections.title: Agreeing and disagreeing
sections.content:
Nuanced ways to agree or disagree:
• I couldn't agree more — strong agreement. I couldn't agree more — punctuality is essential.
• That's a valid point — partial agreement. That's a valid point, but we also need to consider the costs.
• I see your point, however — polite disagreement. I see your point; however, the data suggests otherwise.
• With all due respect — formal disagreement. With all due respect, I believe there's a better approach.
• I beg to differ — firm but polite disagreement. I beg to differ — the evidence clearly shows the opposite.

exercises.question: Which phrase expresses the STRONGEST agreement?
exercises.explanation: I couldn't agree more expresses the strongest possible agreement.

exercises.question: 'I beg to differ' is a polite way to:
exercises.explanation: I beg to differ is a formal, polite way to firmly disagree.

exercises.question: Which phrase shows you partially agree but have reservations?
exercises.hint: You accept some of it, not all.
exercises.explanation: That's a valid point, but... shows partial agreement while introducing a counter-argument.

exercises.question: 'With all due respect' is typically followed by:
exercises.explanation: With all due respect is used to politely preface a disagreement.

exercises.question: Which is the most tentative way to give your opinion?
exercises.explanation: I tend to think is a cautious, tentative way of expressing an opinion.

exercises.question: 'From my perspective' is closest in meaning to:
exercises.explanation: From my perspective means 'as I see it' — similar to 'in my view'.

exercises.question: Which phrase introduces a polite counter-argument?
exercises.explanation: I see your point, however acknowledges the other view before presenting a different one.

exercises.question: 'I'm firmly convinced that' expresses:
exercises.explanation: I'm firmly convinced means you hold a strong, definite belief.
